Profile: Kyle Denzin
Position: Shooting Wing / Floor Spacer | Number: 37 | Team: Pretty Good

The Rundown
A shot-maker in the purest, most frustrating sense of the word. At his best, Denzin provides elite spacing and gravity that opens up the entire floor. Currently mired in a historic efficiency slump that would be a red flag if not for the context: the coaching staff is actively encouraging the volume. He isn't just missing shots — he's missing aggressive shots within the flow of the offense, signaling a player with elite "mental amnesia" — the ability to miss 10 in a row and shoot the 11th with total confidence.

Strengths
• Elite Gravity. Even during this slump, defenses cannot leave him. The sheer volume of attempts (14.0 FGA) forces defenders to stay attached, creating lanes for teammates.
• Defensive Playmaking. Unlike many specialists, he doesn't disappear when the shot isn't falling. Averaging 4.0 steals per game is an elite "stocks" rate, showing high-level defensive anticipation and active hands.
• Conditioning & Movement. To find nearly 10 three-point looks per game requires constant off-ball movement. He's a cardio machine who wears down primary defenders.

Areas for Development
• The Efficiency Gap. A season shooting split of roughly 19/15/50 is jarring. While the form is regarded as pure, the results have been absent.
• One-Dimensional Scoring. Currently lacks a reliable counter-move. When the three isn't falling, there's little evidence of a mid-range pull-up or consistent ability to get to the line (only 2 FTA all season).

NBA Comparison
Kelly Oubre Jr. meets Malik Monk
Remember Oubre's early Warriors days? Massive green light, elite athleticism, high-level defensive energy — but started the season 1-for-25 from three. He kept shooting because the system demanded it. Like Oubre, Denzin provides value through steals and energy even when the rim feels covered in Saran Wrap. The ceiling comp is the "Microwave" outcome — when the slump snaps (and with that form, it will), this is a player who can hit six threes in a quarter. A rhythm-based scorer who can carry an offense for 12-minute stretches.
